The leaf shows scattered white/pale powdery circular spots distributed across the entire leaf surface. The spots appear as discrete, roughly circular patches with a white-gray powdery coating, characteristic of fungal mycelium on the surface. The leaf itself remains green and structurally intact — no necrosis, dieback, or black sooty coating.

This matches Powdery Mildew: discrete white powdery colonies on the leaf surface, not sooty black (ruling out Sooty Mould), no tip/margin necrosis (ruling out Die Back), and no dark sunken lesions (ruling out Anthracnose).
